English: Wooden Palisade
A basic ring of sharpened logs and timber, hastily erected as a first defense atop the hill, providing rudimentary protection and a sense of communal unity for the clan.
Earthen Rampart
Mounds of earth reinforced with timber, forming a solid barrier against attackers. The rampart increases the defensive capability and allows for greater population sheltering within the hillfort.
Hilltop Watch
A simple watch post of raised logs and platforms allowing early sight of invaders. This increases the clans ability to respond to threats and improves overall security.
Stone Reinforcement
Stones are quarried and added to the ramparts, creating a much stronger, weather-resistant perimeter. This innovation marks a transition to more permanent fortifications.
Stockaded Gate
A fortified entrance constructed from heavy timber and reinforced with ironwork, enabling better control of access and defense against sudden raids.
Timber Tower
A tall wooden tower rises above the ramparts, giving sentinels a commanding view and archers an advantageous position, further improving defensive readiness.
Defended Hall
The central hall is fortified, serving as a rallying point and place of last defense for the chief and his retinue, while housing larger gatherings to foster clan unity.
Chiefs Bastion
A formidable bastion for the chieftain, built with thick stone walls and wooden walkways, signifying both authority and security for the clans leadership.
High Watchfort
A towering fortification dominating the landscape, equipped with multiple watchtowers and reinforced gates. The hillfort becomes a true center of Baltic power and defense.
Baltic Hillfort

The final evolution of the Baltic hillfort: a mighty, stone-walled complex with advanced defenses, storerooms, and command towers. The stronghold inspires the clan and anchors its power for generations.
